newsitem.title: USA: US cities urge IRS to withdraw yield burning rules.
newsitem.headline: US cities urge IRS to withdraw yield burning rules.

text.p: U.S. cities plan to urge the IRS to withdraw its proposed rule that tells localities how to avoid "yield burning" and to "level its guns" at bond dealers instead, a key association said on Wednesday.

The National League of Cities, in comments it is set to deliver at an Internal Revenue Service hearing on Thursday, said the rule violates Congress' unfunded mandates law, unfairly targets innocent municipalities and has made cities the victims of "vulture" accountants offering aid in calculating what they supposedly owe the IRS.

The proposed rules, issued on June 26, set up a "rebuttable presumption" that localities paid fair market price for U.S. Treasuries bought with tax-exempt bond proceeds if they get three bids from dealers and dealers have no "material interest" in the offering.

The League said a rebuttable presumption creates major compliance burdens for cities. If Treasury pushes ahead with the rule, it should grant localities that meet certain standards a "safe harbor" from liability, the testimony says.
The cities said the IRS should not make them pay for the actions of dealers.
